full_name: Corey Byrnes | Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University
bio: Corey Byrnes is an associate professor in the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures and in the Comparative Literary Studies Program at Northwestern University, where he researches and teaches classes on the environmental humanities, modern and contemporary Chinese literary and visual culture, animal studies, and spatial and landscape studies. He is the author of Fixing Landscape: A Techno-Poetic History of China’s Three Gorges (Columbia University Press, 2019), which won the Weatherhead East Asian Institute’s 2018 First Book Prize and an honorable mention for the American Comparative Literary Association’s 2020 Harry Levin Prize.
